significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that models possess an abstract, magnitude-separable dimension code yet sometimes fail to consult it, with that failure causally producing the specific “right number, wrong unit” behavior; this is a form-(ii) causal claim of the separable-representation plus patching-repair shape, not a general law. It establishes both a cross-domain error phenomenon and a mechanism distinguishing internally unavailable unit information from a “know-but-dont-check gap,” thereby fixing the explanation of dimensional errors but not predicting other reasoning failures; work on reasoning faithfulness such as Turpin et al. (2023), “Language Models Don’t Always Say What They Think,” and Lanham et al. (2023), “Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning,” makes that availability-versus-use distinction consequential, though this claim remains bounded to dimensional consistency. The negative branches are informative and determinate: a “purely lexical signal” rejects an abstract dimension representation, while chance decoding on error steps favors genuine not-knowing over failed consultation, so verified true and false describe distinct mechanisms. Under topic substitution, generic efficient-reasoning interpretability would not earn this score; the specific abstract-unit/consultation decomposition raises it modestly above the obvious probe-and-steer hypothesis, but its single named failure class keeps it in the 5–6 band.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is the “training-free dimensional-consistency monitor that reads the internal unit-type and flags incompatible operations,” optionally triggering re-derivation; because it operates “at each step boundary,” it is ex ante relative to the final erroneous answer and leaves an action window rather than merely explaining a completed failure. Its asserted task scope spans “physics, engineering, and quantitative science,” medication-style dosing, calculator-augmented reasoning, and tool-use agents, so likely downstream users include system builders and auditors rather than only representation researchers. However, after recalibration on a new model the core conclusion predicts chiefly that a useful dimension representation may be found, not a quantitative ordering, threshold, or scaling relation, and transfer without retraining is posed as a question rather than guaranteed by the hypothesis; thus the monitor may require substantive rediscovery across model families. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic mechanism-based efficient reasoning supplies no comparable unit-aware gating handle, while the claim-specific ex-ante monitor supports the lower edge of the 7–8 band.
